# Repository Instructions

- Every package of this harness: `npx -y @tenphi/harnesspm help`. A package's rules and tools in full: `npx -y @tenphi/harnesspm help <package>`.
- Run a tool: `npx -y @tenphi/harnesspm run <tool> [args]`. Its options: `npx -y @tenphi/harnesspm help <tool>`.
- From outside this folder, add `-C <path to this folder>` before `help` or `run`.

## Workspaces

These folders have harness rules of their own in their `AGENTS.md`: `apps/convention`, `apps/reference`, `packages/docs`, `packages/facade`, `packages/renderer`. Read a folder's `AGENTS.md` before you change files in it.

## @tenphi/eslint-plugin-tasty

- Always-on rule: Linting Tasty styles — After you change styles, Exceptions. Read it with `help @tenphi/eslint-plugin-tasty` (tasty-lint:rules/usage)
- Docs: node_modules/.harnesspm/docs/tasty-lint/llms.txt (tasty-lint:docs)
- Tool: `tasty-lint:check` — Lint files or folders with only the tasty/* rules, as the project's Oxlint or ESLint config sets them (else the recommended preset, or --strict), and print each problem with its rule's page (tasty-lint:scripts/check)
- Edit files with your file tools, not shell commands such as `sed`, so the hook that checks each edit runs (tasty-lint:hooks/check-edit)

## @tenphi/harnesspm

- Always-on rule: Files generated by harnesspm — Never edit outputs, Run sync after a change. Read it with `help @tenphi/harnesspm` (harnesspm:rules/generated-files)
- When editing `harnesspm.json`, `harnesspm.local.json`, `harness/**`, read node_modules/.harnesspm/pkgs/@tenphi/harnesspm/harness/dev.harnesspm/rules/harnesspm-config.md — How to change harnesspm configuration and harness files safely (harnesspm:rules/harnesspm-config)
- Docs: node_modules/.harnesspm/docs/harnesspm/llms.txt (harnesspm:docs)

## Entropy — implementation and local reviews

- Follow [the Entropy rule](.claude/rules/entropy.md) during implementation. Introduce only complexity justified by validated requirements, prefer safe simplification in the affected area, and record material tradeoffs and developer-accepted exceptions.
- Every local code or UI review follows [the repository review procedure](.claude/skills/review/SKILL.md), including an Entropy assessment with a change level relative to the affected context. A [focused Entropy review](.claude/skills/entropy-review/SKILL.md) can run from the diff, repository sources and task context without environment setup, tests or probes. Existing implementation verification duties remain in force.

## Validation

- Treat every ESLint warning as a required fix. Run `pnpm lint` and require zero errors and zero warnings before finishing changes; CI and the release gate enforce this through `--max-warnings 0`. The same requirement applies after `pnpm lint:fix`.
- Fix the underlying issue instead of weakening rules or increasing the warning allowance. Narrow ignores are allowed for intentional shared-style spreads, build-only SVG encoding, and native properties without an equivalent Tasty shorthand. Put a specific reason beside each ignore, preserve style ownership and customization, and verify the affected behavior. Do not add blanket file or rule exemptions to clear warnings.

## Styling architecture

- Root selectors may use stable CSS classes (including `className` on a component root) or `data-component` when an attribute is clearer. Keep existing root hooks when they serve global style ownership or integration. Do not use authored classes for sub-elements or modifiers: use Tasty `data-element` identities for anatomy and data modifiers/state maps for conditions. Never use `data-element` as a modifier or to classify variants; keep identities in structural `$` selectors. Third-party sub-element classes are allowed only when meaningfully unavoidable; document the library, necessity, and scope beside the integration and report them in the task or PR.
- In sub-element property maps, use ordinary states for the owning root (for example `diff`) and `@own(...)` only for the selected element. Do not repeat structural `$` paths inside state maps. Use supported parent states for ancestor conditions; if Tasty cannot represent the required scope, consolidate the smallest verified condition in a named shared state instead of repeating complex selectors across declarations.
- Add global state aliases only for shared semantics that remove repeated logic. Use the `@sm`, `@md`, and `@lg` width scale with boolean negation for narrower layouts. Use native pseudo-class conditions (for example `:popover-open`) and a direct media condition for a single component's threshold.
- Buttons must keep the same position and dimensions on hover. Use color, fill, border color, or shadow for feedback; never add hover translation, scaling, or spacing changes. Minimal buttons share outline button geometry and use `border: "#clear"`.

- Keep each built-in component's style definition in its owning `components/<Name>.styles.js` module. Use `defineComponent(name, options)` for rendered roots and `extendComponent(name, base, options)` for inheritance. Both helpers resolve partial theme overrides inside the engine before CSS extraction. Shared bases own their defaults and must expose a registered customization name. Component markup imports its owner directly; do not restore the `GlobalStyles`, `LayoutComponents`, or `TastyComponents` aggregators.
- Initialize document foundations from the common page shell, independently of replaceable Header/Head components. Reserve `useGlobalStyles()` for document foundations and named generated-content bridges; register those rules during rendering, never on module import. MarkdownContent owns its generated-content bridges, and CodeGroup collects its code/syntax bridges when rendered independently.
- Use shared predefined states for appearance rules: `@light` and `@dark`, including in rules that style the document root itself. Keep scheme media queries in `tasty-states.js`, not individual style trees.
- Tasty and Glaze configuration and style evaluation are build/server-only. Ship extracted static CSS, never Tasty/Glaze browser runtimes, serialized theme configuration, style registries, or hydration initialization. Keep `tastyIntegration({ islands: false })`. Use small client scripts for interactions on server-rendered markup; client islands must not import Cookbook styling, Tasty, or Glaze. Verify this boundary in real consumer builds, including custom themes/components.
- The rendered documentation site must ship only CSS generated by Tasty and Glaze. Do not add CSS files, Astro `<style>` blocks, inline `style` attributes, or CSS modules. Express component styles with `tasty()` and shared global rules with `useGlobalStyles()`. The one exception is behavior CSS that UniAria applies at run time and never in the built HTML: inline positioning and anchor styles, `touch-action` on pressable parts, and the scroll-lock stylesheet Dialog adopts in an anonymous `@layer` while open.

## Behavior layer

- UniAria (`@uniaria/core`, `@uniaria/elements`) is the behavior layer for overlays and tabs: state, keyboard, focus, ARIA and dismissal. Move an overlay's or a tab group's behavior to it instead of extending Cookbook's own scripts. Every Cookbook-owned custom element uses the `cookbook-*` prefix, including passive wrappers. `client/elements.ts` registers UniAria behaviors with `defineElement(definition, { prefix: "cookbook" })` on server-rendered markup; never import the `@uniaria/elements/<name>` entries, which register `uni-*`.
- Cookbook's styles bind to the state attributes UniAria writes. Keep each component's parts marked as UniAria expects (`data-uni`, `data-uni-part`, `data-element`), and do not reuse a UniAria part name for other anatomy inside a UniAria-backed `cookbook-*` element.
- In new or modified style groups, model related descendant and pseudo-element rules as named Tasty sub-elements inside their owning `tasty()` or `useGlobalStyles()` style object (for example, `Label: { $: "> span", ... }`). Do not split component anatomy across additional `useGlobalStyles()` calls with composed selectors.
- Keep sub-element `$` selectors structural and never target their containing element. Prefer Tasty element-name shorthand such as `Primary > Search` for owned `data-element` identities. Put pseudo-class and attribute conditions in property state maps, using `@own(...)` for the selected element's state and ordinary states for the root. Preserve conditional omissions and selector-list differences instead of adding unconditional resets. Use built-in `data-element` identities for owned markup instead of adding anatomy classes or `data-tasty-anatomy`. Model heading levels and other variants in property state maps rather than pretending they are sub-elements.
- When a sub-element's `$` ends in a pseudo-element, `@own(...)` describes the pseudo-element itself and accepts only states it can have. Keep conditions on the element the pseudo-element belongs to in `$` (for example `a[rel="next"]::before`). Empty legacy customization hooks may retain their original conditional selectors with a specific compatibility ignore until their override scopes can be preserved in state maps. Do not use this exception for new anatomy.
- For a change to one spacing edge, let the owning `blockMargin` or `blockPadding` consume start/end tokens and change the relevant token in a state map. Do not use native one-sided spacing properties or lint ignores to patch the cascade. Reset shared margin tokens on each element so they do not inherit into descendants.
- Own renderer markup and behavior without importing vendor component styles.
- Every styled Cookbook component and every new or modified owned global/vendor bridge must support user customization through `theme.styles.<ComponentName>`. Accept only a partial Tasty style object from the user and merge it into the complete base style object inside the engine with `mergeStyles(baseStyles, configuredStyles)`. Use `defineComponent()` or `extendComponent()` for component roots and `resolveComponentStyles()` for global style trees. Register new names in `COOKBOOK_COMPONENT_NAMES`, publish every named Tasty sub-element in `COOKBOOK_COMPONENT_SUB_ELEMENTS`, and document the complete sub-element list for every configurable surface.
- Apply registered semantic typography roles with Tasty's `preset` property. Do not reproduce a preset by referencing its individual `$*-font-*` tokens or wire modifier internals such as `$bold-font-weight` by hand; use modifier syntax such as `preset: "strong"` or `preset: "h2 / strong"`.
- All component colors must use semantic theme color tokens. Expose every new color role through `theme.palette`, resolve it through Glaze for every supported scheme and contrast mode, and update the public types, schema, documentation, and tests. Do not hard-code presentational color values in components.
- Show the brand as a simple Glaze `from` declaration in theme configuration examples. Show other palette colors as relative or absolute Glaze declarations using `tone`, `base`, `contrast`, and saturation factors where needed. Literal color shorthand and structured brand hue/saturation/tone remain supported.

## Documentation

- The reference site has two tabs, set in `apps/reference/docs.config.ts`. **For humans** is short: the home page, how to start, and pages with prompts for a coding agent and the decisions that stay with a person. **For AI agents** has every step: its start page (`docs/agents.md`), the guides and the reference.
- A fact lives in one place. A page for humans says what to ask and what to decide, then links to the guide with the steps. Every prompt names Cookbook; a prompt for a repository without Cookbook also says how to create the site and links to its steps.
- `docs/llms.txt` indexes the docs that ship in `@tenphi/cookbook`, for agents and for harnesspm. List every new English page there; `packages/facade/src/harness.test.ts` checks it.

## Agent harness

- `packages/facade/harness/` ships in `@tenphi/cookbook` for projects that use [harnesspm](https://harnesspm.tenphi.me). It is for agents that use Cookbook; the rules for working on Cookbook stay in this file.
- Its `plugin.json` extends `@tenphi/tasty`, `@tenphi/glaze` and `@tenphi/eslint-plugin-tasty`. harnesspm resolves them from the facade's folder, so they stay facade dependencies even though no facade module imports them (knip ignores them there). Its `docs` is the packaged `docs/` folder, indexed by `docs/llms.txt`.
- `rules/usage.md` (`cookbook:rules/usage`) is always on in every consumer's agent: keep it short. Its title and `##` headings are its summary in `AGENTS.md`, and consumers patch sections by heading, so a renamed heading breaks their patches.
- The patches replace Glaze's "Where colors come from" and "Checking a theme" and Tasty's "Checking styles", so the tools read a site's theme, and the lint plugin's "After you change styles", which needs a `tasty.config.ts` built with `createValidationConfig(docs.theme)` in a site. `theme.mjs` loads `docs.config.ts` with `createColorTheme()` from `@tenphi/docs` and `configureTastyTheme()` from `@tenphi/renderer`, as a build does. `plugin.json` also replaces Glaze's `glaze-theme` skill with `harness/skills/glaze-theme/`, the steps for a site's `theme.brand` and `theme.palette`; it keeps the upstream skill's `name`. `harness.test.ts` guards the dependencies, the patched sections, the replaced skill and the module; `pnpm check:packages` and `pnpm check:install` check the packed files and an installed site.
- `harnesspm.json` changes the harness for this repository only. It trusts the three upstream packages and patches their rules and Cookbook's own rule for work on this repository, as UI Kit does.
- Upstream workarounds, each with its removal condition:
  - The lint patch and `docs/agent-harness.md` send sites on TypeScript 7 to `.js` or `.mjs` style modules, because the lint tools parse `.ts` with typescript-eslint, which needs TypeScript below 6.1. Remove the advice when [eslint-plugin-tasty#171](https://github.com/tenphi/eslint-plugin-tasty/issues/171) is resolved.
  - harnesspm applies a package's patches and replacements to every workspace that uses the patched package, not only to workspaces that depend on Cookbook. So the facade's patches mark their Cookbook steps with "In a Cookbook site" and keep the generic step, the skill and the Glaze patch name Glaze's own skill for other Glaze code, this repository's `harnesspm/patches/glaze-colors.patch.md` says that pointer does not apply to `palette.ts`, and the monorepo paragraph of `docs/agent-harness.md` says so. Drop the pointers, the repository patch's note on them and the paragraph's caveat when [harnesspm#65](https://github.com/tenphi/harnesspm/issues/65) is fixed and Cookbook uses that release.
  - Both Tasty patches and `docs/agent-harness.md` say that `tasty:styles` does not check `#color` or `$token` names. Remove the note when [tasty#473](https://github.com/tenphi/tasty/issues/473) is fixed and Cookbook uses that release.
- `.agents/skills/` is a folder with one link per skill, not a link to `.claude/skills/`, so harnesspm can add its skill links there on any checkout. Add `.agents/skills/<name>` → `../../.claude/skills/<name>` with each new repository skill.
- `pnpm install` runs `harnesspm sync`; `pnpm add` does not. After `pnpm add`, or a change to the harness, `harnesspm.json` or `harnesspm/patches/`, run `pnpm exec harnesspm sync` and commit the changed `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `harnesspm.lock.json` files. CI runs `harnesspm sync --check` and `pnpm check:harness`; `prepack` runs `harnesspm check` for the facade.
